question: How many of Tokyo's 31 health-center districts will exceed the influenza "alert" threshold (10 cases per sentinel institution) in the most recent weekly surveillance report as of October 2, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class anchors: Tokyo 2026 W37 citywide 9.53 -> 14/31 districts >10.0, and Tokyo 2026 W4 citywide 13.83 -> 23/31. Fitting those two points gives a lognormal district spread (sigma~0.48) that reproduces both exactly and lets me map any citywide value to a district count. I reconstructed W37's actual 31-district vector from raw per-health-center case counts (weeklyhc.do) plus the 14 published values, confirming districts are densely packed at 6-10, so counts move fast with the citywide level. Growth: national +68.3% W36->W37 (3.29->5.54), Tokyo 1.49 (W34) -> 9.53 (W37); I take ~1.40x for W38 -> citywide ~13.3 -> ~22-24 districts. But the operative report is more likely W39 (Sep 21-27): the weekly index flags only W38 as delayed (Mon Sep 28) and states a default Thursday cadence, putting W39 at Thu Oct 1, inside the cutoff. W39 has three weekday holidays (Sep 21/22/23); Ehime's 2025-26 New Year weeks (1190 -> 443 -> 661) imply a reporting factor ~0.5 at ~2 open days, ~0.65 scaled to 2.5 open days, which roughly cancels one week of growth and lands W39 near 16-18 districts. No prediction market prices this contract (checked Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold; only US-CDC influenza markets exist), so no crowd anchor. Main downside risk: a bigger holiday suppression or an early plateau of this unusually early AH1pdm09 wave; main upside risk: W38 being the operative report with growth still near 1.6x.

Alert crossed more than a month earlier than the prior season (2025 W43).
GROWTH, FALLING/SUPPRESSING DIRECTION: multi-holiday weeks mechanically depress 定点当たり報告数 because the denominator is sentinels, not clinic-days; MHLW explicitly cautions that 年末年始 医療機関の休診・受診控え produce an apparent drop. Ehime 2025/26 weekly patient totals (pref.ehime.jp/site/kanjyo/124151.html): W50 2,037 -> W51 1,728 -> W52 1,190 -> W1 443 -> W2 661 -> W3 719; the W52->W1 ratio is 0.37 against an underlying trend of ~0.75/wk, implying a reporting factor near 0.50 for a week with roughly 2 open clinic-days, with a ~1.5x rebound the following week. Week 39 2026 has ~2.5 open clinic-days versus ~5.5 in a normal week. Separately, three days of school closure (Sep 21-23) removes the main amplification setting for school-age children, and with a 1-2 day incubation some of that shows up in the same week's Thu-Sat diagnoses. Also note Okinawa, the earliest-starting prefecture this season, is at 16.61 — a ceiling reference for how high an early-season wave has run so far this year.

calls.reference_class: Tokyo 東京都感染症週報 week-over-week transitions during an ascending influenza wave, mapping the citywide 定点当たり報告数 to the number of the 31 health-center districts above 10.0 (calibration weeks: 2026 W37 = 9.53 -> 14; 2026 W4 = 13.83 -> 23), combined with Japanese prefectural sentinel series in multi-holida

calls.reasoning: Resolution almost certainly reads Week 39 (Sep 21-27), not Week 38: Tokyo IDSC posts Thursday of the following week (W37 ended Sep 13, posted Thu Sep 17), W38 is flagged for Mon Sep 28 only because its compilation week holds the holidays, and W39 has no delay note so falls on Thu Oct 1 - exactly the W18(Mon May 11)/W19(Thu May 14) precedent. I put ~88% on W39, ~10% on W38, ~2% on W37 (=14) if W38 slips. Week 39 contains the Sep 21/22/23 holidays (first 5-day Silver Week since 2015), leaving ~2.5 clinic-day-equivalents vs 5.5; the structurally identical GW week W19-2026 cut national ARI 57.69 to 36.32 (x0.63) against a rising trend, and a day-weighted model with weekly growth decaying from 1.745 to ~1.45 plus a ~1.15 post-holiday pile-up puts W39 citywide near 10.5 (W38 near 13.5). Mapping citywide to district count with a curve anchored on W37-2026 (9.53 -> 14) and sloped on W43-2025 (10.37 -> 14) / W4-2026 (13.83 -> 23) gives ~17 for W39 and ~25 for W38. Main counterargument: if the pile-up compensates more than GW-ARI suggests, or growth holds at 1.6-1.75, W39 citywide clears 14 and the count runs 25+; conversely a strong artifact plus deceleration drops it below W37's 14. No prediction market prices this (checked Polymarket/Manifold via harness, Kalshi/bookmakers via search - none found).

- Over all Tokyo weekly reports in 2025-26 and 2026-27 whose citywide value fell in 9.5-14: three observations - W43-2025 citywide 10.37 -> 14 districts (top: 文京 19.29, 中野区 18.90, 池袋 18.50; 14th 八王子市 10.33; Tokyo press release 2025-10-30); W37-2026 citywide 9.53 -> 14 districts; W4-2026 citywide 13.83 -> 23 districts (top 町田 25.38, 八王子 24.56, 中野区 23.20; Tokyo press release 2026-01-29). Implied slope across the 2025-26 pair: ~31 districts per log-unit of citywide value.
- Over those same three weeks conditioned on a TIGHT district spread (the 2026-27 condition now known to hold): W37-2026's 14 above-threshold values span only 10.48-17.31, a narrower log-spread than W43-2025 (10.33-19.29) or W4-2026 (10.33-25.38); a tight spread makes the district count more responsive to a given change in the citywide figure in either direction.
- Over holiday reporting weeks with Mon-Tue-Wed holidays: national 急性呼吸器感染症 定点当たり W17-2026 56.35 -> W18-2026 57.69 (Apr 29 and May 3 holidays, ~4.5 clinic days, 34 prefectures still increasing) -> W19-2026 36.32 (May 4/5/6 holidays, ~2.5 clinic days), a x0.63 step that the reporting service attributed explicitly to 「連休中に医療機関を受診する患者が減少したことに伴う見かけ上の減少」 (rescuenow, 2026-05). Clinic-day ratio over that same pair was 2.5/4.5 = 0.556.

BOTH-DIRECTION FACTORS:
- Upward: seven straight weeks of growth at 1.7-2.0x; the 2025-26 analogue crossed from the 10-line (W43, Oct 2025) to the 警報 line (>30 citywide) within about three weeks (Tokyo press release 2025-11-13); Tokyo's Sep 17 advisory raises testing/consultation propensity; holiday gatherings over Sep 19-23 add transmission whose cases present from ~Sep 23; schools are in session through Sep 18.
- Downward: Week 39 loses Mon-Wed clinic days entirely; schools closed Sep 21-23 removes the main transmission setting for three days; the citywide denominator (419 sentinels) is not adjusted for closures; Sat Sep 19 (in Week 38) opens the 5-day break so some Week 38 sentinels close early; public advisory may reduce mixing; the 15th-ranked district in W37 is below 10.0 and its value is unpublished, so the lower half of the distribution is unobserved.

calls.reference_class: Tokyo weekly 東京都感染症週報 reports in the 2025-26 and 2026-27 seasons with a published citywide 定点当たり in the 9.5-14 range, and the count of the 31 保健所 districts above 10.0 in each (W43-2025: 10.37 -> 14; W37-2026: 9.53 -> 14; W4-2026: 13.83 -> 23)

calls.reasoning: Two observed 2026 pairs (citywide 9.53 -> 14 districts in wk37; 13.83 -> 23 at the winter peak wk4) are both reproduced by a normal across-district distribution with CV 0.435, giving N = 31*Phi((mu-10)/0.435mu); this saturates slowly, so counts near 31 require citywide ~25+ and are very unlikely. Status quo is 14. Tokyo grew 5.46 -> 9.53 (x1.75) into wk37 with national at x1.68, so a wk38 report (full school week, no holidays) plausibly lands near citywide 14 -> ~23 districts. If instead the wk39 report (Sep 21-27) is the latest one posted by Oct 2 - which the site's stated Thursday-evening cadence makes somewhat more likely than not - two more weeks of growth are offset by three lost clinic weekdays over the 5-day Silver Week, giving a similar median but a much fatter left tail (a genuine reported dip below the current 14 is possible). Small residual mass sits on the wk38 report itself slipping past Oct 2, which would leave wk37's 14 standing. No prediction market prices this.

calls.reference_class: Consecutive weekly Tokyo 感染症週報 reports during a rising influenza wave, anchored on the observed citywide-to-district-count mapping for Tokyo's 31 health-center districts (2026 wk37 and 2026 wk4 pairs), with persistence of the last published count as the naive anchor

calls.reasoning: Status quo is 14 districts (W37, citywide 9.53). The operative report is most likely Week 39 (Sep 21-27): all three runs independently read the index's 『原則として、毎週、木曜日の夕方に掲載されます』 plus a ※ note delaying only W38 to Mon Sep 28, and W37 (ended Sep 13) did post Thu Sep 17 — a 4-day lag, contradicting the background's '10-11 days'. W19-2026 posting on its normal Thursday three days after the Golden-Week-delayed W18 is a direct precedent, so W39 on Thu Oct 1 clears the Oct 2 cutoff (~80%). W38 alone would be strongly up: ~1.45x growth on 9.53 -> citywide ~13.5-14 -> ~22-24 districts. But W39 contains three weekday holidays (Sep 21/22/23, first 5-day Silver Week since 2015), leaving ~2.5 clinic-day-equivalents against an unadjusted 419-sentinel denominator; the structurally identical W19-2026 national ARI week ran x0.63 against a flat trend, so ~1.3x underlying growth times ~0.62 artifact gives W39/W38 ~0.8, citywide ~11 -> roughly 18-19 districts. Median 19 therefore sits between the strong-up W38 branch and a suppressed W39 print, with a real left tail (a reported dip at or below 14 needs only the artifact at its strong end, ~20% of mass) and a right tail capped by the fact that 8 districts stayed under 10.0 even at last winter's 13.83 peak — 28+ would require a citywide level above any Tokyo week this season and above Okinawa's 16.61. Market check: I have no retrieval this run; all three runs searched Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi and bookmakers and found no contract on Japanese/Tokyo sentinel surveillance (Polymarket's flu markets are US-CDC-based, matching neither threshold, source, nor deadline) — no crowd anchor, so none applied.
calls.reconciliation: Four substantive disputes. (1) Which report is operative. Runs 1 and 2 put W39 clearly ahead (Run 2 ~88%); Run 3 said only 'somewhat more likely than not'. The factual core — index cadence text, the W38 ※ note for Mon Sep 28, W37 posted Thu Sep 17, W18(Mon May 11)/W19(Thu May 14) precedent, no note on W39 — is reported identically by all three and contradicts the question background's '10-11 day' lag claim; I side with the index text the runs actually read and set W39 ~80%, W38 ~16%, W37-stands ~4%, slightly below Run 2's 88% because no run could find an announced W39 date and a second slip cannot be excluded without retrieval. (2) Size of the Silver-Week reporting artifact. Run 2's national ARI W18->W19 x0.63 (3 weekday holidays, clinic-day ratio 0.556) and Run 1's Ehime New Year reconstruction (~0.5 at ~2 open days) are independent and agree on 0.5-0.7; Run 3 acknowledged the mechanism but let growth dominate its median anyway. I treat the artifact as real and material — this is the main reason my median sits below Run 3's 23. (3) The citywide->district-count slope. Run 1's reconstructed W37 district vector (dense cluster at 7.9-9.6) implies ~4-5 districts per unit citywide; Run 2's W43-2025 point (10.37 -> 14, same count as 9.53 -> 14) implies almost none locally. This is FACTUAL but unsettleable here: Run 1's vector is a reconstruction, not published district values, and the two anchors come from different seasons with different dispersion. I did not pick a side — I used an intermediate slope and let the disagreement widen the distribution rather than shift it. (4) Whether the count can print below 14. Run 3's 10th percentile of 14 effectively denies it; Run 2's 7.5 requires citywide falling below W37. Reconciled: W39/W38 ~0.8 means a print below 14 needs the artifact at its strong end together with weak W38 growth — possible but not the modal path, so ~20% of mass at <=14 and a 10th percentile of 11 rather than Run 2's 7.5 or Run 3's 14. Both bounds are closed; no escape mass declared.

Not fully settleable — no run found an announced W39 date — so ~16% is left on W38 and ~4% on W37 still standing.

disagreements.claim: The question background's statement that PDFs appear '10-11 days after each reporting week ends' is accurate.
disagreements.verdict: Contradicted. W37 ended Sep 13 and was live by Sep 17-18 (IDSC 更新日 Sep 18, ward pages citing W37 updated Sep 18) — a 4-day lag. W38's Sep 28 date is an 8-day exception, not the norm. Runs 1 and 2 both flagged this; Run 3's retrieved index text agrees.

disagreements.claim: Week 39's three weekday holidays will mechanically suppress the reported 定点当たり value by roughly a third relative to trend.
disagreements.verdict: Supported by two independent analogues retrieved by different runs: national ARI W18->W19 2026 x0.63 against a flat trend with an explicit official attribution to holiday consultation decline, and Ehime's New Year weeks implying ~0.5 at ~2 open clinic days. Applied at ~0.62 against ~1.3x underlying growth. Run 3's near-dismissal of this is not supported by any counter-evidence in its own dossier.

disagreements.claim: How steeply the district count responds to a change in the citywide figure near 10-12 per sentinel.
disagreements.verdict: Could not be settled without retrieval. Run 1's reconstructed W37 district vector implies a steep ~4-5 districts per citywide unit; Run 2's W43-2025 anchor (10.37 -> 14, identical count to 9.53 -> 14) implies a nearly flat local slope. Run 1's vector is reconstructed rather than published, and the anchors span different seasons. I used an intermediate slope and widened the distribution instead of choosing.
No real dispute: Run 1 ~1.40, Run 2 ~1.45 decaying, Run 3 ~1.47 implied. Carried forward at ~1.45 (citywide ~13.8), consistent with the observed decay from 1.745 and the national 1.68.

disagreements.claim: Whether the reported count can fall below the current 14.
disagreements.verdict: Yes, but it is not the modal path. Reconciled W39/W38 ratio of ~0.8 puts W39 citywide near 11, above W37's 9.53; a sub-14 print needs the artifact at its strong end plus weak W38 growth. I take the reading I would bet on: ~20% of mass at 14 or below, so a 10th percentile of 11 — above Run 2's 7.5 and well below Run 3's 14.

disagreements.claim: Whether any prediction market prices this contract.
disagreements.verdict: None found — three independent searches (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers) plus the harness title search all returned nothing on Japanese/Tokyo sentinel influenza surveillance. No crowd anchor exists; no blending performed.
